title: Compose, tenants, API keys and a usage ledger
goal: Containerise the gateway, add Postgres, and make every request belong to a tenant: API keys stored as SHA-256 hashes, a usage ledger in tokens written idempotently with a daily rollup in the same statement, and a paginated usage API.

changes.note: Two-stage build; runs as the unprivileged node user; exec-form CMD so SIGTERM reaches node.
Adds gateway and postgres; services reach each other by name through Compose DNS.
tenants, api_keys (hash as primary key), usage_ledger (request_id primary key), usage_daily.
Three lab tenants: acme (gold), globex (standard), noisy (free).
authenticate() with a short in-memory cache, idempotent recordUsage(), keyset-paginated listUsage().
Bearer key to tenant; the same 401 for missing, unknown or revoked keys.
Requires a tenant; bills ok, cancelled and failed requests for the tokens actually generated.
Keeps node_modules, dist and the models out of the build context.

run.label: Stop stage 1's container and dev server, then start this stage
run.cmd: ./scripts/download-models.sh && docker compose up -d --build && docker compose ps

verify.label: A tenant's request is billed
verify.cmd: curl -s localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-lab-acme-0001' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi."}],"max_tokens":16}'
verify.expect: A chat.completion JSON with a "usage" object (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens).

verify.label: The ledger has the row
verify.cmd: docker compose exec postgres psql -U app -d llm -c "SELECT tenant_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, source, status FROM usage_ledger ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 3"
verify.expect: Your request as tenant_id acme, source interactive, status ok, with the same token counts as the response.

verify.label: Idempotency: the same request id twice moves nothing
verify.cmd: docker compose exec postgres psql -U app -d llm -c "WITH ins AS (INSERT INTO usage_ledger (request_id, tenant_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, status) VALUES ('demo-1','acme','m',10,5,'ok') ON CONFLICT (request_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING 1) SELECT count(*) FROM ins"
verify.expect: count 1 the first time you run it, count 0 every time after: a retried write is a no-op.

verify.label: Keys are stored hashed
verify.cmd: docker compose exec postgres psql -U app -d llm -c "SELECT key_prefix, left(key_hash, 16) AS hash, tenant_id FROM api_keys"
verify.expect: Three rows with prefixes like sk-lab-acme- and 64-character hex hashes; the full keys appear nowhere in the database.

verify.label: Paginate the usage API
verify.expect: {"object":"list","data":[...2 rows...],"nextCursor":"..."}; pass that value as &cursor= to get the next page. nextCursor is null on the last page.

concepts.how: Multi-stage image, non-root user, PID 1 receiving SIGTERM so in-flight streams drain.
Compose's embedded DNS is service discovery: the gateway connects to llm-1 and postgres by name, never by IP.
Tenants, keys, an append-only ledger and a rollup table: model the money first.
(tenant_id, created_at DESC, request_id DESC) serves the usage page and its keyset cursor with one index range scan.
Ledger insert and rollup update in one statement (a CTE): both change or neither does.
request_id as primary key + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: retries and redeliveries can never double-bill.
Cursor (keyset) pagination instead of OFFSET on /v1/usage.
API keys as bearer tokens, hashed at rest; the revocation delay is the auth cache TTL.
A bounded pg pool per gateway: pool size x instances must fit under max_connections.

checkpoints.text: docker compose up brings up gateway, llm-1 and postgres, and the gateway is healthy.
A request without a key gets 401; with sk-lab-acme-0001 it is served and appears in usage_ledger.
I ran the duplicate ledger insert twice and saw count 1, then 0.
